paper_title: Light Dark Matter Search with Ionization Signals in XENON1T
suggested_experiment_name: XENON1T (Light Dark Matter Search with Ionization Signals)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on the y-axis (canonical axion-photon coupling)
notes: Paper presents multiple DM model constraints (SI/SD DM-nucleus scattering, DM-electron scattering, dark photons, ALPs) but no single coupling type dominates. Figure 5 shows 6 separate exclusion plots with different y-axis variables: (A) SI DM-nucleon σ [cm²], (B) SI DM-nucleon σ*m_φ⁴ [cm²(MeV/c²)⁴], (C) SD DM-neutron σ [cm²], (D) DM-electron σ [cm²], (E) g_ae (axion-electron), (F) κ (dark photon kinetic mixing). Table I provides specific excluded points but each row uses a different coupling variable. Without a single dominant coupling type, extraction confidence is low. To properly extract limits, separate JSON objects should be generated for each coupling type (AxionElectron for panel E, DarkPhoton for panel F, etc.), but the instruction requires a single coupling_type field. The paper's primary contribution is methodological (S2-only analysis) rather than a single new coupling constraint. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Panel (E) shows axion-like particle (ALP) constraints. The exclusion boundary (black solid line) traces the 90% CL upper limit on g_agamma vs dark matter mass m_a. The plot shows XENON1T's constraint (this work) in black, compared to other experiments (CDMSNT, PandaX-II, CAST, EDELWEISS-III in magenta/red). The boundary exhibits a characteristic minimum around 10 GeV/c² and rises at both lower and higher masses. Sampling is denser near the minimum (7-14 GeV/c²) where the slope changes, and sparser in the linear regions at low and high mass. The y-axis label indicates g_agamma in units of GeV^-1.
